newsitem.title: UK: Dollar regains footing after overnight stumble.
newsitem.headline: Dollar regains footing after overnight stumble.

text.p: LONDON, July 29 (Reuter) The dollar regained its footing after a bout of profit-taking overnight weakened it from Monday's peaks against other major currencies.

It is expected by traders to take another run at setting fresh seven-and-a-half-year highs above the 1.85-mark level it fell shy of yesterday if reports this week confirm the U.S. economy is growing at a healthy pace without stoking inflation.

Sterling, which has tumbled as much as 2.5 percent against the mark since yesterday, was the other key focus for traders. The speed of its fall triggered concern that the one-year rally which took it to multi-year peaks against the mark may be over.

"Sterling and the dollar are the key today," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank in London. "There is not that much interest to sell dollars and if we get good data and a significant upmove in the Dow, this could take dollar through the roof."
Sterling will take longer to recover but should prove more resilient than traders expect, he said.

"Yesterday was a big day for sterling and people are now calling for a top in the pound," Ferridge said. "Yesterday's retracement was a sharp one but we should form a bottom and move back up given that nothing fundamental has changed."

The dollar was at 1.8362/65 marks at 0757 GMT from 1.8470/80 late Monday in Europe. It climbed as high as 1.8490 yesterday, its strongest since November 1989. Dollar/yen was at 117.65/75 from 117.60/70 at yesterday's European close.
Sterling/mark was at 2.9960/70 marks from 3.0130/40 late yesterday while cable was at $1.6316/27 from $1.6321/26 on Monday.

The U.S. employment cost index at 1230 GMT is expected by analysts to have risen 0.8 percent in the second quarter after climbing 0.6 percent in the first quarter. Confirmation that inflation is in check would bolster U.S. assets and the dollar.

Expectations that the U.S. central bank is not about to raise the target fed funds rate from 5.5 percent have intensified in the wake of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony last week.
"Greenspan's recent comments were so relaxed that you have to ask how big a ECI is needed to change Fed expectations," said Joe Prendergast, head of currency research and strategy at CSFB.
The dollar will also be bolstered if a report at 1400 GMT shows U.S. consumer confidence held firm in July, analysts said.
Sterling/mark's plunge yesterday could, however, presage a broad rebound in the German unit, Prendergast at CSFB said.
"The move in sterling/mark is worrying as it could be a warning of a broader mark correction," the CSFB analyst said.

Dollar/yen remained relatively insulated from such concerns, though, and proved resilient in the face of criticisms U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky levelled against Japan on Monday. She said the U.S. automotive trade deficit with Japan had widened and that Japan had fallen short of fulfilling an accord to open its market.
"There was the hint of trade tensions overnight, but this did little more than cap dollar/yen," said Ferridge at Commerzbank.
